Define block-production-use triggers for stale rows, missing rows, schema drift, quota exhaustion, provider incident, and silent semantic changes.

Phase 7c requires separate explicit approval and a reviewed schema-first implementation-design slice after remaining Phase 7b blockers are closed or explicitly accepted.

next_steps: Use this artifact as the routing source for SR-PROVIDER-001 after the reviewed AAPL / MSFT stable retry.
Do not run additional provider data by default; first choose one blocker track and obtain explicit user approval if the track needs any new access or endpoint calls.
A safe next docs-only slice is license / storage / retention review for FMP and SEC audit artifacts, because it can narrow blocker scope without fetching data.
A safe next schema-first design slice is fallback / incident / stability playbook, because it defines production-blocking behavior without consuming provider data.

limitations: This artifact is a plan-only blocker router; it performs no web research, provider contact, token request, trial request, paid access, yfinance check, endpoint call, full-market download, adapter work, DataHub work, runner change, broker automation, or ship-gate claim.
The AAPL / MSFT stable retry is treated as access / response-shape evidence only; it is not provider selection, provider ranking, production readiness, or Phase 7c authorization.
SEC EDGAR success is treated as public fundamentals audit feasibility for two symbols only; it is not a price source, strict free-float source, or alpha-validation result.
FMP remains blocked for implementation until coverage, license, PIT, price adjustment, SEC audit scope, fallback, stability, and production-readiness gates are separately resolved.
